questiontext.text:
Solve the following system of simultaneous equations:

\(\displaystyle {@eq1@} \quad \quad (1)\)

\(\displaystyle {@eq2@} \quad \quad (2)\)

\(x= \) [[input:ans1]][[validation:ans1]]

\(y= \) [[input:ans2]][[validation:ans2]][[feedback:prt1]]

questionnote.text:
The two simultaneous equations are {@eq1@} and {@eq2@}

Solution to the equations: \(x=\){@ta_x@},\(y=\){@ta_y@}

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

falsefeedback.text: It looks like you swapped the solutions for \(x\) and \(y\).

truefeedback.text:
Worked solution:

Using the elimination method, we want to eliminate one of the unknown terms in the equation, either the \(x\)-term or the \(y\)-term. To do this we need to multiply each of the original equations by a constant such that the value of one of the unknown terms adds or subtracts to zero when you add or subtract the two equations.

For example, we can eliminate the \(y\)-term from the equations as follows. First, we multiply equation \((1)\) by {@y_const_eq1@} and equation \( (2)\) by {@y_const_eq2@}, so that we obtain

\({@eq6@} \quad \quad (3) \)

\({@eq7@} \quad \quad (4) \)

Note that equation \((3)\) and equation \((4)\) have {@relation_y@} \(y\)-terms. Next, we {@operation_y@} equation \((4)\) {@prepos_y@} equation \((3)\) to obtain

\({@eq8@} \quad \quad (5)\).

Note that equation \((5)\) is in terms of \(x\) only. Solving for \(x\) we obtain

\(x={@ta_x@}\).

Finally, we we need to substitute our answer \(x={@ta_x@}\) in one of the two original equations to find the value of y. If we substitute it in equation \((1)\), we obtain:

\( {@coef_x_1@} \times {@SP(ta_x)@} {@S(coef_y_1)@}y={@rhs_1@}\)

\( {@coef_x_1*ta_x@} {@S(coef_y_1)@}y={@rhs_1@}\)

\( {@coef_y_1*y@}={@rhs_1@} {@S1(-coef_x_1*ta_x)@}\)

\( {@coef_y_1*y@}={@rhs_1-coef_x_1*ta_x@}\)

\( y={@ta_y@}\)
